title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Robert Jay Josett, 35, a former Costa Mesa police officer, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors: unauthorized computer access and fraud, annoying and repeated phone calls, and contempt of court for violating a restraining order. Over nine months he contacted his mistress thousands of times by text, phone, and social media, sometimes more than 100 times a day. After she ended their relationship in April 2024, he threatened to reveal explicit photos and repeatedly called her and her new boyfriend, up to 58 times in one day, and drove by her home.

Between June and December 2023, Josett made 13 inquiries in a law enforcement database that were not related to his job, about his mistress, someone she dated, and his wife. He also used a license plate reader system to track her and romantic rivals, including in June 2024 after being placed on leave. He was arrested after violating an emergency protective order. He spent nine months on GPS monitoring. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52 week domestic violence program. His certification review is pending.
